claims.text: A tungsten-rich refractory coating on steel rollers and guide plates will significantly reduce corrosion by molten aluminum.
A silicide-based refractory coating on steel rollers and guide plates will significantly reduce corrosion by molten aluminum.
The proposed coating will extend component service life by at least a factor of two relative to uncoated steel.
Conventional steel rollers, pulling rollers, and guide plates are used in high-temperature hot-dip aluminum plating operations.
A tungsten-rich refractory material can be deposited as a surface layer using an advanced cladding method.
Pack cementation can produce the proposed tungsten-rich or silicide-based layer on steel.
The applied layer will be dense and adherent.
The applied layer will form a stable diffusion barrier on the steel surface.
The refractory surface layer will isolate the steel substrate from direct chemical attack by molten aluminum.
The refractory coating will resist dissolution in molten aluminum.
A refractory surface material can resist high-temperature oxidation through formation of a stable surface barrier.
The coating will limit aluminum infiltration into the underlying steel.
Limiting aluminum infiltration will reduce corrosive wear of the steel substrate.
Uncoated steel components undergo severe and rapid erosion during prolonged molten-aluminum exposure.
Coating performance depends on coating composition, thickness, and integrity.
Coating performance depends on exposure temperature, immersion time, and molten-bath composition.

Coated and uncoated steel coupons can be compared under the same molten-aluminum exposure using mass change, microscopy, thickness loss, interfacial chemistry, surface damage, and mechanical-property retention.
Failure to reduce corrosion or measurably improve service life relative to uncoated steel would falsify the hypothesis.
